title: Add locality-aware RBAC templates, KMS residency proxy, and audit harmonizer
author: Priya Rao
release_notes: Introduces locality-aware RBACv2 templates and a lightweight KMS residency proxy; harmonizes audit sampling for cross-region flows. Default behavior is opt-in behind the 'locality-policy' feature flag. No customer-facing API changes. Admins should review RBAC templates before enabling.
description: Motivation: Customers operating across multiple regions require both RBAC constraints that can express geography-bound roles and a safe way to pin encryption to region-scoped KMS keys while preserving audit fidelity. Existing rule sets were ad-hoc and caused operator confusion when KMS fallbacks happened in a different geozone. This PR introduces three cooperating components: 1) a compact RBACv2 policy template DSL (rbac/templates) that can express locality constraints and inheritance; 2) a lightweight KMS residency proxy (pkg/kms/residency-proxy) which validates requested key regions and emits provenance headers; and 3) an audit harmonizer (telemetry/audit/harmonizer) that normalizes and samples residency-related events to reduce noise while preserving compliance proof points. Summary of changes: - rbac/templates: new template language, examples for 'tenant-region-restricted' and 'operator-cross-zone-read' templates, template compiler and unit tests. - pkg/kms/residency-proxy: authorization checks to ensure CMK usage matches request residency claim, region affinity caching, and explicit denial path on mismatch. - telemetry/audit/harmonizer: layered sampler that groups similar residency-deny events and emits canonical compliance records suitable for export. - sdk hooks: minor additions to Python/TS SDKs to pass the new residency headers for private deployments. - docs: operator guide and migration notes under docs/security/residency-and-rbac.md Design notes: - Policy templates are intentionally compact (YAML-first) and compile to the existing RBACv2 JSON model to avoid runtime changes to the enforcer. - Residency proxy is implemented as a transparent gRPC middleware for Dedicated/Private deployments and as an optional sidecar for on-prem installers. - Audit harmonizer retains full raw payloads for 90 days (configurable retention) but reduces long-term export volume via deterministic sampling and canonical event stitching. Compatibility & rollout: - Feature gated under 'locality-policy' feature flag. - Default: disabled for hosted customers; opt-in via console or env var for Dedicated/Private. - Migration path: admin tool 'rbacctl compile --validate' added to validate templates against tenant metadata. Testing & CI: - Unit + integration tests cover template compilation, residency assertion matching, and audit sampling correctness. - Benchmarked residency-proxy latency ~0.7ms median added to tokenized requests (see bench results in PR artifacts). Checklist: - [x] Template language spec and examples - [x] Residency proxy core logic + caching - [x] Audit harmonizer deterministic sampler - [x] End-to-end integration test (synth tenant, kms mock, audit sink) - [x] Docs and operator migration notes - [x] SDK header passthrough - [x] Backward compatibility: templates compile to RBACv2 JSON - [x] Feature flag gating Rollback plan: flip feature flag off; residency-proxy responds in permissive passthrough mode that emits a deprecation warning header; compiled templates not applied if flag is off. Security considerations: - Residency proxy enforces KMS principal mapping and performs strict validation of encryption-context to mitigate key misuse. - All provenance headers are HMAC-signed before insertion into audit stream. - Audit harmonizer preserves raw events for compliance audits. Observability: new per-tenant metrics: residency_denies_total, residency_proxy_p95_latency_ms, audit_harmonizer_stitched_events_total. Migration notes for operators: run 'rbacctl dry-run --templates ./my-templates.yml' to see impacts; enable flag in staging first. Related: ENG-2314 (template compiler), SEC-89 (audit sampling policy).
